iupacName: 1,2-dimethylbenzene (o-xylene); mixture of ortho, meta, para isomers
environmentalPersistence: Moderate — atmospheric half-life ~1–2 days; soil persistence moderate

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — slightly less than toluene due to lower volatility and bioavailability
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Moderate — chloroplast membrane disruption similar to benzene/toluene but less acute
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate — margin necrosis; less severe than benzene

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → yellow-green → brown margins; nearly identical to toluene visually
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate orange — toluic acid and MDA signature

synergies.synergyNote: Part of the BTEX indoor VOC cluster — xylene contributes to the combined GSH depletion load; slightly less reactive than benzene/toluene individually

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Paints, varnishes, adhesives, gasoline, printing inks — common in art classrooms and workshops
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Moderate-high — CNS depressant; irritant; reproductive concerns at chronic exposure
educationalContext.climateLink: Component of urban VOC emissions contributing to tropospheric ozone formation
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — art supplies indoors; traffic outdoors
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: In art supplies and markers used in school — highly relevant to classroom air quality discussion
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Art room air quality, urban smog, VOC regulation

sources: Heiden AC, et al. (1999). Emission of volatile organic compounds from ozone-exposed plants. Ecological Applications, 9(4), 1160–1167.
EPA (2012). Xylenes: Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS). US Environmental Protection Agency.
Ugrekhelidze D, et al. (1997). Uptake and detoxification of o-xylene by Pelargonium hortorum plants. Plant Science, 123, 163–169.
